# FDG7059

> DO provide (at least) these common constructors on all exceptions. Make sure the names and types of the parameters are exactly as shown in the following example.

Framework Design Guidelines, 3rd edition, section 7.4 Designing Custom Exceptions.

## How it is checked

- Check: sdk (partial coverage)
- Diagnostics: CA1032
- Automatic fix: yes
- Severity: library warning, application warning, test warning
- Status: verified

CA1032 reports an exception type that lacks a public parameterless, (string message) or (string message, Exception innerException) constructor, internal exceptions included. It does not ask for the protected serialization constructor of the example, which .NET 8 made obsolete (SYSLIB0051, see FDG7058), so coverage is partial. Its code fix adds the missing constructors, which changes no existing signature. Not library only, because the text says "on all exceptions", and CA1032 reports internal exceptions too. The test profile stays warning, since an exception type declared in test code is thrown and caught like any other, and the fix only adds constructors.

## From the book

```csharp
public class SomeException: Exception, ISerializable {
  public SomeException();
  public SomeException(string message);
  public SomeException(string message, Exception inner);

  // this constructor is needed for serialization.
  protected SomeException(SerializationInfo info, StreamingContext
context);
}
```
